attribution.note: Zitron states and endorses the proposition in his own commentary.

semantics.note: The surrounding passage firmly asserts unprofitability. The hedge concerns why coverage omits profits. The normalization preserves the descriptive computing claim without adding an explicit causal assertion.

contract.note: General provider losses, including development and operating expenses, are an ordinary reading in context. Using 2023 follows the surrounding revenue discussion. Neither universal losses nor negative gross margins are required.

evidence.note: Relevant retrospective company accounts available before the cutoff. Anthropic's GAAP loss includes substantial valuation adjustments; it does not establish comparable sector-wide losses or computing expenses.
A contemporaneous company disclosure of extensive training resources. It provides relevant computing context, but no representative sector expense measurement or profitability finding.
The report concerns OpenAI's 2022 loss, outside the contract's 2023 period. It cannot establish the targeted year's profitability.

Contemporaneous reporting of a profitable provider is relevant counterevidence, although its profit definition and period are unspecified. One exception does not contradict the contract's general claim; computing expenditure is also reported.

reviews.rationale: The packet lacks representative, comparable 2023 accounts establishing substantial overall losses or general profitability. Anthropic's accounts and Midjourney's reported profitability concern individual providers; OpenAI's reported loss is from 2022. Computing demands have contextual support, but the combined sector-wide observation remains unsettled.
